title: Observability signal maturity and dashboard deprecation guidelines
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a pragmatic signal maturity model plus concrete deprecation guidelines for dashboards and metrics in the observability space. The goal: reduce dashboard sprawl, keep core SLOs/SLIs healthy, and provide a clear migration path for lower-value signals so teams can focus on high-impact telemetry.

Audience:
- Eng teams that own services (serving-runtime, platform, console)
- Observability maintainers and infra platform engineers
- Product/ops stakeholders who rely on dashboards for incident response

High-level approach (one-liner):
Classify each signal (metric/span/dashboard) with a maturity tier, attach minimal metadata (owner, SLO/alert linkage, maintenance cost), and apply automated cleanup or archiving rules after a review window.

Signal maturity model (recommended tiers):
- Tier 0: Ephemeral / scratch signals
  - Created for short-lived experiments, no longer than 30 days without owner sign-off.
  - Example: ad-hoc histogram of a new feature toggle latency used during a spike test.
  - Action: auto-expire.
- Tier 1: Team-internal diagnostics
  - Useful for debugging, low cardinality, limited audience. Not used in SLOs.
  - Example: per-shard cache eviction counters, internal queue depth for background task processor.
  - Action: keep for 90 days rolling retention, document owner, mark as non-public.
- Tier 2: Service health signals (recommended retention + dashboard)
  - Core availability/performance indicators, used in oncall runbooks or postmortems.
  - Example: request.rate, token.latency.p50/p95, error.rate, model_fallback_rate.
  - Action: 1y retention, tied to SLOs, explicit alert definitions.
- Tier 3: Business/Customer-facing metrics
  - Product KPIs that may be surfaced to GTM/CS. High bar for changes.
  - Action: long retention and change-control process.

Minimum metadata to attach to every signal (enforce via PR template):
- owner: team+person
- description: 1-sentence intent
- tier: 0/1/2/3
- sla/slo_link: Jira/Confluence reference or empty
- cost_note: estimated scrape cardinality / high-cardinality tag list
- dashboard_links: list of dashboards referencing the signal
- retention: days

Concrete metric definitions (samples to copy into metric registry):
- infra.request.count
  - type: counter
  - description: number of incoming API requests to the inference gateway
  - tags: service, region, route
  - owner: eng-platform / Diego Alvarez
  - tier: 2
  - retention: 365

- inference.token.latency_ms
  - type: histogram (p50/p95/p99 buckets)
  - description: server-side token generation latency (microsecond precision trimmed to ms)
  - tags: model, model_variant, route, seq_len_bucket
  - owner: eng-serving-runtime / Priya Nair
  - tier: 2
  - retention: 365

- kv_cache.hit_ratio
  - type: gauge
  - description: fraction of requests served from prefix/KV cache (0..1)
  - tags: model, shard, cache_tier
  - owner: eng-serving-runtime / Oliver Jensen
  - tier: 1
  - retention: 90

- batch.size_distribution
  - type: summary
  - description: batch sizes observed at the batching layer (p50/p90/p99), helps tune batching config
  - tags: model, pool, latency_slo_class
  - owner: eng-runtime / Maya Chen
  - tier: 1
  - retention: 90

Tracing: naming, sampling & retention guidance
- Span naming convention (flat tokenized inference stack):
  - <svc>.request           - top-level API gateway handling
  - <svc>.inference.exec    - runtime model call (includes quantization path name in attribute)
  - <svc>.cache.lookup      - prefix/KV cache check
  - <svc>.batch.collect     - batching aggregation window
  - <svc>.model.kvcache.hydrate - background KV cache population
- Essential attributes to attach to every span: request_id, client_project, model, model_variant, seq_len, tokens_returned, batch_size, route, sampled_policy
- Sampling policy:
  - Default: adaptive head-based sampling that ensures 1 trace per 10k requests plus priority sampling on error traces and any trace where token.latency > p99
  - For Tier 2 signals: increase sampling to capture 1 in 100 traces for the top 3 production routes to ensure regressions are detectable.
- Retention: keep full traces for 14 days, store aggregated span metrics (counts/latency histograms) for 90 days.

Dashboard lifecycle and deprecation criteria
- Dashboard classification: "incident", "daily-observability", "capacity-planning", "team-playground"
- Deprecate when ALL of the following are true: 
  1) no views in last 90 days (dashboard platform metric), AND
  2) all referenced signals are Tier 0 or Tier 1 (i.e., not SLO-backed), AND
  3) owner does not object within 14 days of notice.
- Migration process:
  - Automated scan (monthly) produces a candidate list + email to owners.
  - Owner can either: (a) upgrade signals to Tier 2 and provide SLO linkage, (b) request archival window 90/180 days with reason, (c) approve deletion.
- Change control: any deletion or major redesign of a Tier 2/3 dashboard requires a short RFC (one page) and at least one cross-team reviewer.

Alert budget and grouping guidance
- Each service should have an alert budget (alerts per oncall per week) default = 10. Track via Alerting::budget dashboards.
- Prioritize SLI->SLO first: alerts should map to SLO burn (page only if immediate action required).
- Alert grouping: include route/model/region as grouping keys to reduce noise but keep at most two dynamic labels to avoid cardinal explosion.

Operational runbook snippets (copyable)
- High inference latency (p95 token generation > 500ms and model_fallback_rate > 1%)
  - Check: recent kernel selection changes (link PRs), autoscaling events in Dedicated pools, and batching config changes.
  - Temporary mitigation: shift traffic to fallback variant (route-level policy), increase autoscale target by +20% for 10 minutes.

- Cache degradation (kv_cache.hit_ratio < 0.6 and cache.populate_errors > 0)
  - Check: cache shard redis health, background hydrate job logs, recent model rollouts that changed prefixes.
  - Mitigation: pause cache invalidations, trigger full hydrate for affected shard.

Open questions / TODOs (working list)
- How do we capture model-quality regressions as a signal without leaking PII? Proposal: store prompt-hash-level eval counters and synthetic eval runs per rollout.
- Need a lightweight UI in Console for teams to self-serve tier changes and attach SLO links. (ENG-3210)
- Decide default adaptive trace sampling targets for low-traffic routes (<1rps) to avoid over-retention.

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Run the automated scan by 2026-04-01 and send beta list to owners.
- Add metric PR template to metric-registry repo that enforces minimal metadata.
- Schedule a 30-minute sync with platform/product to align on Tier 3 gating.

References and helpful links:
- Metric registry (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Metric+Registry
- Tracing guidelines RFC: ENG-2099
- Dashboard lifecycle automation: ENG-2751

End of note.

(Informal — rough bullets, some unresolved items. Keep this in Drive as a working doc.)
